column1: # THE LEDGER ROWS (2026-10-22, PLAN row 64): the consumer's production rule, the coupling of the
# volatility with the price and the correction rate, read on each set's volatility-state window the
# way `ledger_readings_of` reads a path. Scored by the gap ledger and the search's ledger objective;
# `ledger_row_tests` re-derives the shipped literals (`ledger_records`) from this file.
# vol-exit Nx edge H/C pts/yr     the simple volatility exit of `volexit-2026-10-20.tsv` with its two
#                                 thresholds moved: hold the index below H%, cash at the DFF rate at or
#                                 above C% of the sample sd of the last 24 daily simple returns of the
#                                 printed close; the rule's log growth less the leg held, points a year,
#                                 on the index (1x) and on a 3x leg reset daily (3x). The production pair,
#                                 1.5/2.0, is `volstate-2026-10-20.tsv`'s own and not repeated here
# vol-exit spells a century       at 1.5/2.0: the out spells (maximal runs of sessions in cash), every
# vol-exit time out %             one, the spell open at the window's end included; the share of
# vol-exit median spell sessions  sessions out; the median spell's length
# vol-exit avoided/missed a spell over the closed spells, the mean per spell, 100 x log, for each leg:
#   1x pts, 3x pts                the leg's fall from the exit to the spell's low (0 if it never fell)
#                                 and its rise from that low to the re-entry; a leg wiped out inside a
#                                 spell avoided ruin (+inf) and missed nothing (0)
# vol-exit whipsaw spells %       the closed spells over which the 1x leg rose
# vol-exit cash earned pts/yr     the short rate over the out sessions
# vol-exit held crash pts/yr      the 1x leg's log losses on held sessions down 5% or more (negative)
# vol coupling monthly corr       over whole non-overlapping 21- and 63-session blocks from the window's
# vol coupling quarterly corr     first session: corr(r, the change in lv), r the block's log return, lv
#                                 0.5 ln of its mean squared daily log return
# up-day vol slope in falls       the slope of the up days' own lv change on r over the 21-session blocks
# declines 10%+ a century         the declines of 10% or more from the running peak (peak, trough,
#                                 regain) per century at 252 sessions a year, one still under water at
#                                 the window's end included and a deep one counted once however many
#                                 dips it holds, on the price the daily log returns compound to
# return lag-1 autocorr           the demeaned lag-1 autocorrelation of daily log returns over the
#                                 sessions after 1999-03-10 alone (the correction leaves it about zero
#                                 before the cut); the model's on the last n sessions of each path, n
# Banded like `volstate-2026-10-20.tsv`'s rows: 20000 one-year-block resamples (`NumPyRng`, seed
# 20260918), each session's inputs kept together, read at `RECORD_BAND_PCTS`; jointC, jointLo and
# jointHi a joint band at 0.05 over each family (`LEDGER_FAMILIES`: the surface, the parts, the
# coupling, the declines, the one-day reversion; the reversion's resamples are its own window's).
# Only the coupling rows' and the reversion's bands are read (`model@`); the others are judged by
# where the record falls among the model's histories (`record@`).
# nasdaq  the long tech record of `volstate-2026-10-20.tsv`: Ken French's daily HiTec industry through
# sp500   the CRSP market total return of `volexit-2026-10-20.tsv` (Mkt-RF + RF, its signal and its
# LAG-FREE: the computed indexes' daily returns through 1999-03-10 (HiTec, CRSP) are read with the
# stale-price lag removed, an MA(2) inversion fitted per calendar five-year block (`unlag_returns`);
# `-recorded` reads them as printed. QQQ, a fund, is read as printed.
